# PR #4912: Patch: in Duos, BALTHASAR measures "half its starting health" against the 20 a Duos hero starts on, not 30

Closes #4831

## What changed

`query::starting_health_of` now knows about Duos. For a Duos seat it returns the own HP the seat started on, whether or not the seat is spent. Otherwise it returns the seat's handicap `heroHealth`, else `HERO_HEALTH`, as before. In a Duos game, Stinkyscape #18.2 BALTHASAR now votes only at 9 or less of 20, not at 14 or less.

- **Engine.** `DuosLife` has a new field `own_start: Option<i32>` (`ownStart` on the wire). `duos_seat` writes it, so a Glitch re-seat in `sync_pools` writes it again. It is serde-defaulted, so co-op states stored before this change still load. It is left out of the JSON when it equals `DUOS_OWN_HEALTH`, the value every real setup uses, the way `PlayerState.handicap` is. So standard Duos games serialize and hash as before, and 1v1 is untouched. `starting_health_of` checks Duos first, because `duos_seat` sets the hero's health to own HP whatever the handicap says.
- **Second reader.** IA #71 Thermal Throttler also calls `starting_health_of`; the issue missed it. A Duos Throttler now counts missing health from 20. Its set is held (R4577000), so no player sees this yet.
- **Spec.** New ruling `spec/rulings/R4831000.md`: a Duos hero's starting health is the own HP its seat started on, spent or not. R1866002 and R4587004 carry an amendment, §13.4 gets one sentence, and `spec/pending/4831.md` holds the §11 paragraph.

# #4831: Patch: in Duos, BALTHASAR measures "half its starting health" against the 20 a Duos hero starts on, not 30
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

### What happens

Stinkyscape #18.2 BALTHASAR ("Start of turn: Vote to remove you if your hero has less than half its starting health") votes far too early in a Duos game.

Its script (`crates/cards/src/scripts/stinkyscape/c018_2_balthasar.rs:29`) compares `2 × hero health` with `starting_health_of(state, me)`. That helper (`crates/engine/src/query.rs:91-93`) answers the seat's handicap `heroHealth`, else `HERO_HEALTH` (30). It never looks at `PlayerState.duos`. A Duos hero starts on its team's own HP, 20 (`crates/engine/src/duos/state.rs`, `duos_seat`: `side.hero.health = rules.own_health`), and Duos sets no handicap `heroHealth`.

So a Duos seat with BALTHASAR in its backrow, on 14 of its 20 own HP, unspent, with its team's pool whole at 20, gets a vote cast against it at the start of its turn (`2 × 14 < 30`). It votes at any own HP of 14 or less, where half of the real starting health is 10. Once the seat is spent, `hero.health` reads the pool and is still compared with 30, so it votes at a pool of 14 or less.

The vote is one of the three that remove a seat, and a removed seat loses the whole co-op game for its team, with most of the team's 40 life left.

### What should happen

No vote until the hero is below half of the 20 it started with (9 or less).

- §13.2: "Each duel hero starts at its seat's own HP, and each team at its pool (§13.4), instead of at 30 health."
- §13.4: "A seat starts with its team's `own_health` as its duel hero's health", and "Every word for a hero's health reads own HP while the seat is not spent and the pool once it is."
- R1866002: BALTHASAR "compares its controller's hero health with the health that hero started the game with".

### How to reproduce

Two tests fail on `main` (3a83bd7), in [`crates/ai/tests/audit_engine_duos.rs` at 933dd76](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/933dd76b39f8f72c31f19ee5ee3b499ad8274190/crates/ai/tests/audit_engine_duos.rs) (branch `claude/vigilant-mayer-pmyrhr`; the file sits in the AI crate's tests only because that target links the testkit and every card): one in a 1v1 `scenario()` carrying the Duos life `duos_create` sets, one through a real `duos_scenario` game and `duos_reduce`.

```rust
use jackioh_engine::config::DUOS_HUMAN_TEAM;
use jackioh_engine::testkit::PlayerId::{P1, P2};
use jackioh_engine::testkit::*;

const VANILLA: &str = "core-008";
const BALTHASAR: &str = "stinkyscape-018-2";

/// What `duos_create` puts on a duel's side: R82 off, its own HP, unspent, on its team's full pool.
fn duos_side(s: &mut Scenario, player: PlayerId, own: i32) {
    let side = &mut s.state_mut().players[player];
    side.hero.health = own;
    side.auto_end_turn = Some(false);
    side.duos = Some(DuosLife { pool: DUOS_HUMAN_TEAM.pool_health, pool_cap: DUOS_HUMAN_TEAM.pool_health, spent: false });
}

fn balthasar_votes(own: i32, duos: bool) -> usize {
    jackioh_cards::register_all();
    let library = vec[VANILLA; 4];
    let mut s = scenario(json!({
        "active": "p2",
        "p1": { "hand": [VANILLA], "backrow": [BALTHASAR], "health": own, "library": library },
        "p2": { "hand": [VANILLA], "library": library },
    }));
    if duos {
        duos_side(&mut s, P1, own);
        duos_side(&mut s, P2, DUOS_HUMAN_TEAM.own_health);
    }
    s.end_turn();
    assert_eq!(s.state().active, P1);
    s.last_events().iter()
        .filter(|event| matches!(event, GameEvent::VoteCast { def_id, .. } if def_id == BALTHASAR))
        .count()
}

#[test]
fn balthasar_reads_a_duos_heros_starting_health_as_its_own_hp() {
    assert_eq!(balthasar_votes(14, false), 1, "1v1: 14 of 30 is below half");
    assert_eq!(balthasar_votes(9, true), 1, "Duos: 9 of 20 is below half");
    assert_eq!(balthasar_votes(14, true), 0, "Duos: 14 of 20 is above half");
}
```

Output today: `Duos: 14 of 20 is above half   left: 1   right: 0`, and from the real Duos game: `BALTHASAR voted against a hero on 14 of its 20 starting health   left: 1   right: 0`.

### Where

The rules engine: `crates/engine/src/query.rs` (`starting_health_of`), with `crates/engine/src/duos/state.rs` (`duos_seat`) and `duos_life.rs` (`DuosLife`).

### Version or commit

`main` at 3a83bd7.

### Notes for the fix

- Make `starting_health_of` Duos-aware. A duel's side does not know its team's `own_health` today (`DuosLife` holds only `pool`, `pool_cap`, `spent`), so put the seat's starting own HP on `DuosLife`, written by `duos_seat` (so a Glitch reset rewrites it) and serde-defaulted (so stored co-op states still load), and answer it for a Duos seat.
- **A decision the spec does not make**: what a *spent* seat's "starting health" is. Its own 20, or the pool's cap, since its health then reads the pool? That takes a ruling note in this issue's block, amending R1866002, with a proving test (CLAUDE.md rule 3). The Hard AI team's larger pool (`DUOS_POOL_HEALTH_HARD`) is part of the same question.
- R1866002 gives the fallback as "else HERO_HEALTH (30)", but it was written for 1v1 and the tutorial's handicap and says nothing of Duos; neither §13 nor any Duos ruling (R1168000 to R1168003, R964000) says a Duos hero starts at 30.
- `starting_health_of` has one non-test reader, BALTHASAR. The sibling Brains MELCHIOR and CASPER do not read health, and nothing else in `crates/cards/src` or `crates/engine/src` reads a hero's starting health.
- No existing test pins BALTHASAR at 30 in Duos: the card's own tests and `crates/engine/tests/rules/handicap.rs` are 1v1 only, and `crates/cards/tests/cross/duos.rs` has no BALTHASAR test.
- The rest of the Duos engine read sound under the same audit: 26 random co-op games over the whole catalog, each played to a result, with every listed action accepted, pools in agreement, all four views passing the redaction check and every log folding to the live hash.
- A card change in play: it needs its pending patch fragment (`docs/ADDING_CARDS.md`).

## Risks

- **Hashes and replay.** A field that is always serialized would change every Duos `duos_hash` and the TS type. The server's Duos replay checks only the result (`crates/server/src/duos/replay.rs` `open`), so at worst such a game is refused as `rules_changed`, as R767000 accepts for an engine rule change.
- **Stored states.** Server checkpoints are stored `DuosState` JSON. `#[serde(default)]` loads them, and `None` reads as 20, which is right for every live game.
- **Web.** `ts(optional)` keeps `HeroView.duos` assignable from the web's fixtures (`apps/web/src/duos/DuosBoard.test.tsx` builds `{ pool, poolCap, spent }`). A required field would break typecheck.
- **Hidden information.** `ownStart` reaches both seats through `HeroView.duos`. It is public team rules, already shown by `DuosTeamView`.
- **Purity.** No new statics, I/O or hash-ordered collections.
- **Glitch reset.** Between a reset and `sync_pools`, a side has no `duos` and reads handicap/30. No start-of-turn can run inside that window, because `sync_pools` runs in the same reduce.
